notes.text: Help › Open the full guide opens the Coach’s Manual, a searchable guide to every feature.
Invitations now include a quick start guide: coaches get the Coach Quick Start, helpers the Helper Quick Start.
Club library: drills every team can import. In the Library, Show › Club library; Import to my team makes your own draft copy.
Suggest a drill for the club library from its Share dialog: tick Add to the club library.
Admin › Club library (Bench Boss Labs): add or decline requests, add your own drills, remove drills, and give every coach access.

title: Admin: teams set up end to end

notes.text: Admin (Bench Boss Labs account): make a team with a name, logo and colours; the app makes its folder and files in Google Drive.
Add coaches by email: Google emails them a link; they sign in and pick the team’s two files once to join.
Team logo and colours show in the top bar, on printouts, drill sheets and videos, and new players take the team’s colour.
Adopt a team folder made outside Admin, rename a team, and archive a team (removes everyone’s access; nothing is deleted).
Helpers and coaches now pick the team’s shared-plans file rather than a folder, which Google Drive didn’t let them open. Teams set up before 1.5.0: open the team in Admin and tap Update sharing.
Up the ice: turn any drill so the net is at the top (Details › Rink, or the Up the ice button). Labels stay upright, Flip still works, and printouts, sheets and videos show it the same way.

Dump in, next to Pass and Shoot: tap who dumps it, then where it should end up. Into the corner goes straight there; around the boards rims along them, behind the net if it has to. It gets its own step so players can chase it in the next one.
Ringette lines: tick Show ringette lines in a drill’s Details to draw the two yellow lines.
Share on a drill: tick what to send (video, printable sheet, drill file) and send them together with one Make and send.
Nets look like real nets from above, a little larger so they read on a phone.
Publish asks first every time, so nothing goes to the team by accident.
Age groups are now U8/U9, U10, U11, U12, U13 and U14+. Drills tagged with the old groups show the matching new ones.
Sharing a plan is just Share, Send link and Stop sharing. Helpers are managed in Settings › This device › Helpers.
Share on a drill makes a video of it playing (MP4 on most phones), ready to text, WhatsApp or email to anyone.
The drill sheet: one page with the setup, a picture of each step with its caption, and the coaching points. Print it, or Save as PDF to send it.
Send drill file and Import: give a drill to a coach on another team who has Practice Pilot; it arrives in their Library as a copy.
The plan printout has a QR code on each drill card: scan it with your phone to watch that drill play.
Pass lines are drawn so every picture of a drill can be saved as an image or video.
Share on a plan: add your helpers by their Google email once, then share the plan and send them the link.
On their phone, helpers sign in, pick the team’s shared folder once, and see each shared plan’s run sheet with every drill playing, even with no signal at the rink.
Publishing changes to a shared plan, or to one of its drills, updates the helpers’ copy straight away. Stop sharing and Remove are in the Share dialog.
Helpers see plans still to come and from the last 30 days, never drafts or the library. Shared plans show a Shared with helpers label.

title: Your team’s library in Google Drive

notes.text: Sign in with Google in Settings › This device and join your team: pick your team’s library file once, and every coach’s published drills and plans appear on your tablet, PC and phone.

Drafts and Publish: a new drill or plan stays on your device as a Draft until you tap Publish. Changes to a published one wait for Publish changes, and Discard changes goes back to the team’s version.
If another coach published the same drill while you were working on it, Publish asks: Keep mine, Take theirs, or Keep both. Opening a drill someone else is changing tells you so.
The top bar shows when you last synced; tap it for Sync now. The app catches up whenever it opens.
Ice time is now a team setting, and Help explains teams, drafts and publishing.
Coaches can pass, receive and shoot: pass from a player to a coach, a coach to a player, or one coach to another, with the same Pass and Shoot tools.
A coach with a puck on their stick carries it when you drag them, with the wavy “with puck” line.
Drag a player along the route you want and they skate it in that step: loops, curves, around the pylons. A nearly straight drag stays a clean straight line, and the puck on their stick comes along.
Drag the same player again to keep going from where the route ended. Undo, or Stay still in the Piece tab, starts over.
A traced route has dots you can drag to fix one spot, and Straighten takes them all out.

Build and change drills on a phone held sideways. The rink fills the screen, the tools run down the left (+ Piece, Move, Pass, Shoot, Draw), the steps run along the bottom, and Options opens the piece, step and details settings.

Held upright, a phone plays the drill and lets you change its details: title, purpose, setup, coaching points, tags and more. Turn it sideways to move pieces or add steps; nothing is lost when you turn it.
Rink view and Flip are in the ⋮ menu on a phone. A one-time tip suggests adding Practice Pilot to your home screen for a bigger rink.

title: Two passers or shooters in one step

notes.text: A second pass or shot in the same step no longer changes the first one, so two players can pass or shoot at the same time. The Pass and Shoot tools above the rink always ask you to tap the player first, even when a player is selected.
A player without a puck gets a new one on their stick (from the pile beside them, if there is one), instead of taking a puck another player already uses.
Passing or shooting again with the same player in a step says it replaces their earlier pass or shot.
Plans: build a practice from your drills, with minutes for each and start times worked out for you.
Station blocks run two to four drills at once, with groups rotating or staying put, and helpers at each station.
An ice-time bar shows the minutes left and warns when the plan runs over.
The equipment list is counted from the drills, with each drill's setup lines.
Print a plan, or save it as a PDF: a run sheet, then a card for each drill with its picture, purpose, setup, coaching points and who runs it.
Each drill has a usual length, and plans start from it. A drill's preview has Add to plan.
Set your team's ice time in Settings.
Undo messages close when you leave the screen they belong to.

title: Pass and Shoot are easier to find

notes.text: Pass and Shoot are now tools above the rink: tap Pass, tap the passer, then the teammate.
Pass and Shoot always show for a selected player. If the player doesn't have the puck, the nearest puck goes to them first.
A player who receives a pass can shoot or pass it on without undoing the pass.

title: Easier passing and a bigger preview

notes.text: Pass and Shoot: tap the player with the puck, tap Pass and then the teammate, or Shoot and then the spot. A pass goes to where the teammate ends up and waits until they arrive.
Resize the drill preview in the library by dragging the handle beside it, or tap Expand to hide the cards. While a preview is open, the cards shrink to a list.
The Step tab lists what's moving in the step. Everything in a step moves at the same time.
Easier to pick a puck on a player's stick: tap the player again to switch to the puck, or tap Select the puck.

Every drill has a Setup list telling other coaches how to prep the ice, such as "Pucks on both blue lines" or "Pylons on the dots". It shows in the preview above the coaching points, and search looks in it too.
The three sample drills now come with setup lines.
Adding a new coaching point no longer clears the one you just typed.
Build drills that move: place players, pucks and equipment, add steps, and drag players to make them skate, carry the puck, pass and shoot.
Curved paths, stops and pivots, and passes that wait until skaters arrive.
Callouts that follow a player, and a glow on the player to watch.
Draw on a drill with pen, arrows, boxes and text.
Tags, age groups, level, coaching points, video links and goalie notes for every drill.
A library with search, filters and a playing preview, plus three sample drills to start.
Templates, Duplicate, Undo and Redo, and Recently deleted, which keeps deleted drills for 30 days.
The Install button no longer shows once Practice Pilot is installed on your device.
Updated to Bench Boss Labs kit 1.0.1.
Practice Pilot installs on your tablet or phone and opens with no internet, even at a rink with no signal.
Help, with what's new in each update, and a full guide.
Settings › This device: Install (a button, or the steps for your device), your team name, Dark or Light theme, and Back up now / Restore to keep your work safe.
When there's an update, an amber banner says what's in it, with Update now and Later.
